answer: A ferrous stake makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can earn, it must lock scarce collateral, so spawning thousands of sock puppets costs real capital, and proven misbehavior forfeits the stake. Around it, a nebula of peer attestations ties every agent to its work history, so a brand-new identity starts with zero reputation and must earn trust slowly. Each claim carries a cipher signature bound to the staked key, so the same agent cannot reappear under a fresh name without paying the full cost again.
